voice.speaker: odysseus-as-beggar
voice.caption: I had a house and men of my own once, and I gave to any beggar who came. Then Egypt swallowed it. My crew were cut down along the river and I was sold from hand to hand until I came to this door.

voice.speaker: antinous
voice.caption: What god dumped this plague on our dinner? Back from the table, you shameless thing, before you find an Egypt worse than the first.

voice.speaker: odysseus-as-beggar
voice.caption: Your body is handsome, but there is no mind inside it. Sitting in another man's house you would not give a grain of salt from a table that is not yours.

voice.speaker: antinous
voice.caption: Antinous hurls a footstool into his shoulder.

voice.speaker: odysseus-as-beggar
voice.caption: Hear me, gods, and you avengers of the poor, if a beggar has any claim on heaven. Let Antinous meet his death before his wedding day.
Even the other suitors condemn the violation of a stranger.

keys.beat: Odysseus begs from Antinous with a story of his own fall.
Antinous orders the beggar away from the table.
Odysseus answers that his mind is less handsome than his body.
Antinous hurls a footstool into his shoulder.
The beggar stands like a rock
From the threshold the beggar calls on the gods against Antinous.
Even the other suitors condemn the violation of a stranger.
